examples.en: The child grabbed my sleeve and wouldn't let go.
I wiped my tears away with my sleeve.
The sleeve of the hanbok fluttered in the wind.
Kimchi broth got on my sleeve.
The end of the sleeve was frayed, so I took it to be repaired.
The clothes are big, so the sleeves hang down over the backs of my hands.

explain: '소매'가 가장 일상적인 말이고, '소맷자락'은 늘어진 소매 부분을 느낌 있게 말할 때 써요. 한복이나 이야기 속 장면에서 잘 어울려요. 소매의 끝부분만 가리킬 때는 '소매 끝'이라고 해도 돼요.

phrases.en: The sleeves were long, so I rolled them up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 일상적인 말이라서 평소에는 '소매'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most everyday word, so people usually say '소매' in daily speech.

phrases.en: The ends of my sleeves are damp from the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소매의 끝부분만 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer only to the end of the sleeve.

phrases.en: I rolled up my sleeves and did the dishes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 시작하려고 소매를 올리는 모습에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits the image of pushing up your sleeves to start work.

explain_en: The hanging end of a sleeve, a bit literary. '소매' is the everyday word, while '소맷자락' describes the hanging part of a sleeve with more feeling. It suits hanbok and story scenes. To point only to the end of a sleeve, you can also say '소매 끝'.

t90.ax: Kimchi broth got on my sleeve.

examples.ko: 팔에 벌레가 기어가는 것처럼 스멀스멀 간지러워요.
examples.en: My arm feels creepy-itchy, as if a bug were crawling on it.

examples.ko: 등 뒤에서 이상한 기운이 스멀스멀 올라왔어요.
examples.en: A strange feeling crept up from behind my back.
An anxious feeling is slowly creeping up in me.
Smoke crept slowly into the room.
My scalp felt creepy-itchy, so I kept scratching it.

examples.ko: 아침이 되자 안개가 스멀스멀 퍼지고 있어요.
examples.en: As morning came, fog was slowly spreading.

explain: 벌레가 살갗 위를 기어가는 듯 근질근질한 느낌을 말해요. 비유로 불안, 연기, 안개 같은 것이 슬그머니 번지거나 올라오는 모습에도 자주 써요. '스멀스멀 올라오다', '스멀스멀 퍼지다'처럼 어울려요.

phrases.example: 밤이 되자 무서운 마음이 스멀스멀 올라왔어요.
phrases.en: When night came, fear crept up inside me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불안이나 기운이 슬그머니 생겨날 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when anxiety or a feeling creeps up quietly.

phrases.en: Smoke slowly spread through the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연기, 안개, 냄새가 천천히 번질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when smoke, fog, or a smell spreads slowly.

phrases.en: An ant is crawling up my arm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌레가 느릿느릿 기어가는 간지러운 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the ticklish feeling of a bug crawling slowly.

explain_en: It describes a tingly, itchy feeling as if a bug were crawling on the skin. Figuratively it is also used for anxiety, smoke or fog creeping in and spreading. It pairs with '스멀스멀 올라오다' and '스멀스멀 퍼지다'.

examples.ko: 감기가 다 나은 줄 알았는데 재발했어요.
examples.en: I thought my cold was gone, but it came back.

examples.ko: 허리 통증이 자꾸 재발해서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: My back pain kept recurring, so I went to the hospital.
What do we do if the same problem recurs?

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 병이 재발할 수 있다고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor said the illness could come back.
I take my medicine regularly so that it does not come back.
That accident happened again, and everyone was shocked.

explain: '재발하다'는 한 번 나았던 병이나 사라졌던 문제가 다시 생길 때 써요. 병, 버릇, 사고에 어울리고, 처음 생기는 일에는 '발생하다'를 써요. '다시 생기다'보다 의학이나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 약을 꾸준히 먹으면 재발을 막을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you keep taking the medicine, you can prevent a recurrence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이나 문제가 다시 생기지 않게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when stopping an illness or problem from coming back.

phrases.example: 회사에서 사고 재발 방지 교육을 했어요.
phrases.en: The company held training to prevent the accident from happening again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 회사에서 자주 쓰는 딱딱한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal phrase often seen in the news and at work.

phrases.en: That problem came up again.
phrases.nuance_ko: '재발하다'와 비슷하지만 더 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 재발하다 but simpler and more casual.

explain_en: 재발하다 is for an illness, habit or problem that was gone and comes back. For something happening the first time, use '발생하다'. It appears in medicine and news more often than the plain '다시 생기다'.

examples.en: Tears streamed down the child's cheeks.
The cup tilted and the water poured out.
Sweat is running down my forehead.
The candle wax melted and ran down.
Raindrops trickle down the window.

examples.ko: 슬픈 영화를 보다가 눈물이 주르르 났어요.
examples.en: Tears rolled down while I watched the sad movie.

explain: 눈물, 땀, 빗물이 한 줄기로 길게 흘러내리는 모양을 말해요. '주르륵'과 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 계속 내리는 비는 '주룩주룩'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Sweat streamed down my face.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주르르'와 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Interchangeable with '주르르'.

phrases.en: It's pouring rain outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비가 계속 내리는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes rain falling steadily.

phrases.example: 슬픈 영화를 보니 눈물이 주르르 흘렀어요.
phrases.en: Tears streamed down as I watched the sad movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈물이나 땀이 흐를 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often used for tears or sweat flowing.

explain_en: It describes tears, sweat or rain running down in a single stream. You can swap it with '주르륵'. Rain that keeps falling is '주룩주룩'.

t90.ax: Sweat is running down my forehead.

examples.ko: 삼촌이 사고로 척수를 다쳐서 휠체어를 타요.
examples.en: My uncle injured his spinal cord in an accident and uses a wheelchair.
The spinal cord is inside the spine.
The doctor suggested a spinal cord test.

examples.ko: 척수가 손상되면 감각이 사라질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the spinal cord is damaged, feeling can be lost.

examples.ko: 척수에 문제가 생기면 몸을 움직이기 어려워요.
examples.en: If there is a problem with the spinal cord, it is hard to move the body.

examples.ko: 척수의 신경을 다시 살리는 연구가 진행 중이에요.
examples.en: Research on reviving the nerves of the spinal cord is under way.

explain: '척추'는 등뼈이고 '척수'는 그 안을 지나는 신경 다발이에요. 이름이 비슷해도 뼈와 신경으로 달라요. 의료 이야기에서 '척수 손상', '척수 신경'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 척수 손상 환자는 오랫동안 재활 치료를 받아요.
phrases.en: People with spinal cord injuries receive rehabilitation for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고나 병으로 척수를 다친 것을 말하는 의료 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A medical expression for an injury to the spinal cord caused by an accident or illness.

phrases.example: 척수 신경은 척수에서 나와 온몸으로 퍼져요.
phrases.en: Spinal nerves come out of the spinal cord and spread throughout the body.
phrases.nuance_ko: 척수에서 나오는 신경을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the nerves that come out of the spinal cord.

phrases.en: I almost injured my spinal cord when I fell.
phrases.nuance_ko: '척수'에 조사 '를'을 붙여 다치는 몸의 부분을 말하는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows 척수 with the particle '를' as the body part that gets hurt.

explain_en: '척추' is the backbone, and '척수' is the bundle of nerves running through it. The names are similar, but one is bone and the other is nerve. In medical talk you see '척수 손상' and '척수 신경'.

examples.en: I was nervous before the exam, so I took a cheongsimhwan.

examples.ko: 청심환 한 알이면 마음이 좀 가라앉을까요?
examples.en: Would one cheongsimhwan pill calm me down a bit?
You can buy cheongsimhwan at a pharmacy.
The cheongsimhwan didn't make me sleepy.
I might take at least a cheongsimhwan before the presentation.
My grandmother believes cheongsimhwan works.

explain: 한방에서 온 환약으로, 긴장되거나 놀랐을 때 마음을 가라앉히려고 먹는 약으로 알려져 있어요. 시험, 면접, 발표 앞에서 '청심환 먹어야겠다'라고 농담처럼 말하기도 해요. 약이니까 먹기 전에 약사에게 물어보세요.

phrases.en: I took a cheongsimhwan before the interview.
phrases.nuance_ko: 청심환과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb pairing with cheongsimhwan.

phrases.en: I bought one cheongsimhwan pill at the pharmacy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약의 양을 셀 때 '알'을 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '알' to count pills.

phrases.en: I'm so nervous about the presentation. Should I at least take a cheongsimhwan?
phrases.nuance_ko: 긴장될 때 농담처럼, 또는 가볍게 제안할 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual, half-joking way to suggest taking one when nervous.
phrases.en_equiv: Should I at least take a cheongsimhwan?

explain_en: It is a pill from traditional Korean medicine, known as something taken to calm nerves when anxious or startled. People joke '청심환 먹어야겠다' before exams, interviews or presentations. Since it is medicine, ask a pharmacist before taking it.

examples.ko: 췌장은 배 안쪽 깊은 곳에 있는 장기예요.
examples.en: The pancreas is an organ located deep inside the belly.

examples.ko: 건강검진에서 췌장 수치가 조금 높게 나왔어요.
examples.en: My pancreas levels came out a little high in the health checkup.

examples.ko: 췌장에서 인슐린이 나온다고 과학 시간에 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned in science class that insulin comes from the pancreas.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님은 췌장도 같이 검사해 보자고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor suggested we check the pancreas as well.

examples.ko: 기름진 음식을 많이 먹으면 췌장에 부담이 돼요.
examples.en: Eating a lot of greasy food puts a burden on the pancreas.
Managing blood sugar is easier when your pancreas is healthy.

explain: 병원이나 뉴스에서 많이 듣는 장기 이름이고, 병명에서는 '췌장암'처럼 뒤에 말이 붙어요. 혈당과 소화 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Pancreatic cancer is a disease that is hard to find early.
phrases.nuance_ko: '췌장' 뒤에 '암'이 붙은 가장 흔한 병명이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common disease name made by adding 암 after 췌장.

phrases.example: 술을 많이 마시면 췌장염에 걸릴 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you drink a lot, you can get pancreatitis.
phrases.nuance_ko: 췌장에 염증이 생긴 병을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the disease where the pancreas becomes inflamed.

phrases.example: 의사 선생님이 췌장이 안 좋다고 하셨어요.
phrases.en: The doctor said my pancreas isn't in good condition.
phrases.nuance_ko: 췌장 건강에 문제가 있다고 쉽게 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to say there is a problem with pancreas health.

explain_en: This organ name is heard mostly in hospitals and the news, and in disease names it takes a suffix, as in '췌장암' (pancreatic cancer). It comes up often in talk about blood sugar and digestion.

examples.en: Fortunately it's not serious, just a bruise.
I fell on the stairs and bruised my knee.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 타박상에는 냉찜질이 좋다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor said a cold compress is good for bruises.
I collided while playing soccer and got a bruise on my thigh.
Because of the contusion, I got a big bruise.

examples.ko: 가벼운 타박상이라 며칠 쉬면 나을 거래요.
examples.en: They say it's a mild bruise, so it'll heal after a few days' rest.

explain: 부딪히거나 맞아서 피부는 찢어지지 않았지만 속에 멍이 들고 붓는 상처를 말해요. 긁히거나 쓸린 상처는 '찰과상'이라고 해요. 병원이나 뉴스에서 쓰는 말이고, 일상에서는 '멍들었다'라고 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I fell, and now there's a bruise on my arm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에 상처가 생겼다고 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for saying an injury has appeared on the body.

phrases.en: I bought a bruise ointment at the pharmacy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 타박상에 바르는 약을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for medicine applied to bruises.

phrases.en: I bumped hard, and my leg got bruised.
phrases.nuance_ko: '타박상'보다 일상에서 훨씬 자주 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A much more everyday and simple way to say it than '타박상'.

explain_en: Medical — bruise or contusion injury from impact. It is an injury from a hit or collision where the skin is not broken but the tissue beneath is bruised and swollen. A scrape on the surface is called '찰과상'. It is the word used at hospitals and in the news, while in daily talk people may just say '멍들었다'.

t90.ax: I fell on the stairs and bruised my knee.

en: to be slim; to be slender; to be fragile

examples.en: That singer has a delicate voice.
She carried a heavy load on her slender shoulders.
She looks slight, but she's strong.
She spoke in a faintly trembling voice.
My fingers are slender, so rings are too big.
The frail child has become healthy before I knew it.

explain: 몸이나 목소리, 줄기가 가늘고 연약해 보일 때 써요. '날씬하다'와 달리 약하고 섬세해 보이는 느낌이 있어요. 보통 '가녀린 몸', '가녀린 목소리'처럼 사람이나 식물에 말해요.

phrases.en: My wrists are slender, so the ring is too big.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 가늘고 약해 보이는 부분에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: It suits thin, delicate-looking parts of the body.

phrases.en: A flower bloomed on the slender stem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물의 가는 줄기에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It also works for thin plant stems.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 가녀려 보여도 힘이 세요.
phrases.en: That person looks slender but is strong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습의 인상을 말할 때 '~아/어 보이다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '~아/어 보이다' to describe a visual impression.

explain_en: Thin and fragile; literary, stems, wrists, voices. It describes a body, voice or stem that is thin and looks fragile. Unlike '날씬하다' (slim), it carries a feeling of being delicate and weak. It is typically used as in '가녀린 몸' and '가녀린 목소리', for people or plants.

t90.ax: That singer has a delicate voice.

examples.en: A dazzling brilliance came from the jewel.
I polished the shoes hard until they shone.
I want to have glowing skin.

examples.ko: 달빛 아래 호수가 은은한 광채를 띠었어요.
examples.en: Under the moonlight, the lake took on a soft glow.
Even though this painting is old, its brilliance is the same.

examples.ko: 눈부신 광채에 나도 모르게 눈을 감았어요.
examples.en: I closed my eyes without realizing it at the dazzling light.

explain: 그냥 '빛'보다 반짝이며 눈부신 빛을 말해요. '광채가 나다', '광채를 띠다'처럼 쓰고, 눈빛이나 얼굴에서 느껴지는 생기도 비유해요. 물건 표면이 반들반들한 윤기는 '광택'이라고 해서 구분해요.

phrases.example: 그 반지는 불빛 아래에서 광채가 나요.
phrases.en: That ring sparkles under the light.
phrases.nuance_ko: '광채'와 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation with 광채.

phrases.example: 기쁜 날에는 그의 눈이 광채를 띠었어요.
phrases.en: On happy days his eyes shone brightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈이나 얼굴에서 생기가 느껴질 때처럼 비유로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used figuratively, for a lively look in the eyes or face.

phrases.en: The new shoes have a nice shine and look pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건 표면이 반들반들한 윤기는 '광택'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The smooth glossy shine of a surface is called 광택.

explain_en: Rather than plain '빛', it means a sparkling, dazzling light. It is used as '광채가 나다' or '광채를 띠다', and it also figuratively describes the vitality seen in eyes or a face. The smooth shine of a surface is '광택', which is a separate word.

examples.en: The skirt flutters in the wind.
A butterfly fluttered over and landed on my shoulder.
The loose shirt flaps back and forth.
The child runs off with a scarf fluttering behind.
The towels dance on the clothesline.
The hem of the coat fluttered.

explain: 얇은 천이나 가벼운 것이 바람에 자꾸 흔들리는 모양이에요. 뒤에 '날리다, 흔들리다, 움직이다' 같은 동사가 잘 와요.

phrases.en: Her hair flutters in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가벼운 것이 바람에 자꾸 날리는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something light being blown around by the wind.

phrases.en: The laundry sways in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천이 계속 흔들리는 모습에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits cloth that keeps swaying.

phrases.en: A white butterfly flutters away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나비나 새가 가볍게 날개를 흔들며 나는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a butterfly or bird flying with lightly flapping wings.

explain_en: It describes thin cloth or light things moving back and forth in the wind. Verbs like '날리다', '흔들리다' and '움직이다' often follow it.

examples.en: The child is sitting quietly and demurely on the chair.
She sat demurely with her legs together.
The bride bowed her head modestly and greeted everyone.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 어른들 말씀을 다소곳이 들었어요.
examples.en: That child listened meekly to what the adults said.

examples.ko: 꾸중을 들은 동생이 다소곳이 서 있어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling, who got scolded, is standing there quietly.

examples.ko: 손을 모은 채 다소곳이 차례를 기다렸어요.
examples.en: With hands folded, I waited my turn quietly.

explain: 앉다, 서다, 고개를 숙이다, 듣다처럼 조용한 동작과 자주 함께 써요. 얌전하고 공손한 태도를 그릴 때 쓰는 말이라, 소리 내지 않고 조용히 있는 모습에 어울려요.

phrases.en: She sat quietly and modestly on the chair and waited.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말로 얌전하게 앉은 모습을 그려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, picturing someone sitting demurely.

phrases.en: The bride stood there demurely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조용하고 공손하게 서 있는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes standing quietly and respectfully.

phrases.en: The child bowed their head politely and said hello.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예의 바른 인사나 부끄러운 모습에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits a polite greeting or a shy gesture.

explain_en: Describes gentle, quiet posture or manner, often girls or children. It often goes with quiet actions such as sitting, standing, bowing the head and listening. It paints a gentle, respectful attitude, so it suits someone who stays calm and quiet.

t90.ax: She sat demurely with her legs together.

en: to be slippery; to be slimy

examples.en: There's oil on the floor, so it's slippery.
The soap keeps feeling slippery in my hand.

examples.ko: 생선을 만졌더니 손이 미끈거려서 바로 씻었어요.
examples.en: My hands felt slimy after touching the fish, so I washed them right away.

examples.ko: 샤워 후에도 몸이 미끈거리면 물로 더 헹궈 보세요.
examples.en: If your body still feels slimy after a shower, try rinsing more with water.
After I wiped the slippery bathroom floor, it was fine.

examples.ko: 이 샴푸는 헹굴 때 좀 미끈거리지만 금방 없어져요.
examples.en: This shampoo feels a bit slick when you rinse it, but it goes away soon.

explain: 기름, 비누, 점액처럼 물기나 미끄러운 막이 있어서 손이나 몸에 닿는 느낌을 말할 때 써요. '미끄럽다'가 넘어질 수 있는 바닥 같은 데 잘 어울린다면, '미끈거리다'는 닿는 감촉에 더 초점이 있어요. '미끌거리다'도 비슷한 느낌으로 써요.

phrases.en: The handle is slippery because there's oil on it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '미끈거리다'와 거의 같은 뜻의 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A near-synonym of 미끈거리다.

phrases.en: Seaweed feels slimy when you touch it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '느낌'을 꾸며 촉감을 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often modifies 느낌 to describe how something feels.

phrases.en: My hands feel slippery after using detergent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에 닿은 미끄러운 감촉을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a slippery feel on the body.

explain_en: Verb for a slippery or slimy surface; the paired word is an adjective and more vivid. It describes how something feels to the touch when it has a film of oil, soap or mucus. '미끄럽다' fits a floor you could fall on, while '미끈거리다' focuses more on the feel against your skin. '미끌거리다' is used with a similar feel.

t90.ax: There's oil on the floor, so it's slippery.

examples.en: When the mother-in-law and daughter-in-law get along, the home is peaceful.
There are many dramas about conflict between mothers-in-law and daughters-in-law.
My mother-in-law and I get along like friends.
Even between a mother-in-law and daughter-in-law, mutual respect is needed.
On holidays, the mother-in-law and daughter-in-law cook together.
Conversation is important for a mother-in-law and daughter-in-law to grow closer.

explain: 시어머니와 며느리 사이를 말해요. '고부 갈등'처럼 '고부'만 쓰기도 해요. '부자간', '모녀간'처럼 사람 사이를 나타내는 '-간'과 같은 짝이에요.

phrases.en: There are many dramas about mother-in-law and daughter-in-law conflicts.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고부간'에서 '간'을 빼고 두 사람의 다툼을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Drops 간 from 고부간 and is often used for conflict between the two.

phrases.en: The mother-in-law and daughter-in-law seem to get along really well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 사람의 관계가 어떤지 말할 때 '사이'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 사이 to talk about how the two get along.

phrases.example: 시어머니와 며느리 사이는 서로 노력해야 좋아져요.
phrases.en: The relationship between a mother-in-law and daughter-in-law improves when both make an effort.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고부간'을 풀어서 말한 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to spell out what 고부간 means.

explain_en: It refers to the relationship between a mother-in-law and her daughter-in-law. People also say just '고부', as in '고부 갈등'. The '-간' ending works like in '부자간' (father and son) and '모녀간' (mother and daughter).

examples.en: My friend whispered to me behind the teacher's back.
The two people are whispering in the corner.

examples.ko: 모두가 듣는 자리에서 귀엣말해도 되는 분위기가 아니에요.
examples.en: It's not the kind of setting where you can whisper in front of everyone.

examples.ko: 아이는 엄마 귀에 대고 귀엣말하며 웃었어요.
examples.en: The child laughed while whispering into her mother's ear.
Why do you keep whispering while looking at me?
It was a secret, so I spoke softly as if whispering.

explain: '귀엣말을 하다'처럼 띄어서 쓰기도 해요. '속삭이다'는 작은 소리가 중심이고, 귀엣말하다는 상대의 귀 가까이에서 몰래 말한다는 점이 중심이에요. 일상에서는 '귓속말하다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.example: 선생님 옆에서 귀엣말을 하면 다 들려요.
phrases.en: If you whisper next to the teacher, they can hear everything.
phrases.nuance_ko: 띄어 쓰는 형태로, 같은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced form, with the same meaning.

phrases.en: The child whispered to their mother and laughed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귀엣말하다와 같은 뜻이고 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 귀엣말하다, but more common in daily speech.

phrases.en: The two of them laughed while whispering.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)며'로 이어서 다른 행동과 함께 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-(으)며' it links to another action done at the same time.

explain_en: Near-synonym of 귓속말하다 (귓속말하다); whispering right into someone's ear, but the less common word. You can also write it as two words, '귀엣말을 하다'. '속삭이다' focuses on a quiet voice, while 귀엣말하다 focuses on speaking secretly close to someone's ear. In daily speech people also say '귓속말하다'.

t90.ax: The two people are whispering in the corner.
